newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Tractebel to merge with Powerfin.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Tractebel to merge with Powerfin.

text.p: Belgian utility Tractebel is planning to merge with its Powerfin unit, offering one new Tractebel share for three Powerfin shares, the companies said in a statement on Tuesday.
Tractebel is a unit of Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB), itself a unit of French Cie de Suez .
Tractebel currently has about 60 percent of Powerfin, its international energy unit.
Tractebel said in a statement that the exchange ratio offered was fair for both Tractebel and Powerfin shareholders. The offer had been reviewed by three financial institutions.

The reasons for the merger were: simplification of field operations; reduction of overhead costs; tax related savings; a clearer group image; avoidance of potential conflicts of interests; and an increase of market liquidity in the shares.
On a weaker Brussels bourse Tractebel shares closed at 14,800 francs, down 150 francs on the day, while Powerfin stock was at 4,970, down 10 francs.
Based on the closing prices the offer values Tractebel shares at 14,910 francs each, a premium of 0.7 percent over the market price.
Separately, Tractebel said 1996 group net profit rose by 6.7 percent to 12.09 billion Belgian francs ($346.6 million) from 11.34 billion in 1995. Turnover rose to 344.3 billion from 321.7 billion.
The utility proposed raising its 1996 net dividend to 385 francs per share from 370.
Powerfin reported unchanged 1996 group net profit at 7.71 billion francs, but turnover almost tripled to 12.92 billion from 4.91 billion on the back of new projects abroad.
Profit held steady as a result of the financing and development costs and goodwill depreciation related to the new foreign acquisitions.
Powerfin increased net dividend to 121 francs per share from 115 paid in 1995. ($ = 34.88 Belgian Francs)
